learning: Ask whether s-bend progress recovers toward 0.15 to 0.185 with the baseline body and whether s-bend line loss stays at or below 1. If progress stays near 0.13, the wider spread (not the body) is the cause of the progress drop. Also check whether steering_oscillation on the slalom falls below iteration 0's 0.163.
notes: Controller is held at iteration 2's values so the only change against iteration 2 is the body (0.18 m, 0.8 kg). Sensor layout matches the Builder's ±0.03 m, 15 mm spacing, y=0.04 proposal. Expected score near or above 54 is a forecast, not a measurement.
rationale: Iteration 2 changed two things at once: the body (0.18 m to 0.14 m long, 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg) and the controller (kp 2.0 to 2.5, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6 to 1.5). It also moved to the wider spread with the 4 cm row. Its s-bend progress fell from 0.185 to 0.1275, while s-bend line loss dropped from 2 to 1. The Builder now reverts the body to 0.18 m and 0.8 kg while keeping the ±0.03 m spread at 15 mm spacing and the y=0.04 row. To isolate the body variable against iteration 2, I keep the controller exactly as in iteration 2: kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.5, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], and last_direction line loss. Any change in progress or line loss versus iteration 2 can then be attributed to the body. The Builder's sensor_size 0.016 test stays deferred until progress reaches at least 0.15 with line loss at or below 1. Expected score is near or above 54, with s-bend progress recovering toward 0.15 to 0.185. This is an expectation, not a measurement.
